current_answer: Issuer eligibility, signed authorization, service admission, privileged submission and settlement are separate gates. Mint V2 verifyOrder checks a subset; a signature does not reserve capacity. A reverting collateral payout rolls back the same transaction's USDe burn and nonce/counters, not earlier waiting, token-dollar value or bank delivery. The API documents HTTP 200 for both executed and reverted states; RFQ reuse, on-chain nonce consumption and quote/admission/inclusion deadlines are distinct. Signing-wallet validity can be state-dependent. These source/policy findings do not establish current permissions, inventory, receipts or backing adequacy. Claimed sUSDe cooldown output remains USDe and requires its own subsequent issuer or market exit.
summary: Issuer eligibility, signed authorization, privileged submission and the atomic settlement boundary.
